ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised, adopted at the Sixth Session of the Standing Committee of the Fourteenth National People's Congress on 8 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information by Companies (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised, effective 1 July 2024); and applicable People's Bank of China AML/CFT rules for licensed non-bank payment institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or official company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): notarize the certificate if required by local practice; obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority in the source state; present the notarized and Apostilled original to PRC authorities. Route B (non-Hague member state): notarize the certificate; legalize it at the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the source state; present the legalized original to PRC authorities. Route A and Route B are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Status of each foreign corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry administrator or Companies Registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): obtain certified copy or official extract; notarize if required; obtain Apostille from the competent authority in the source state. Route B (non-Hague state): notarize and then obtain legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the source state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the WFOE formation and Power of Attorney executed in favor of the China filing agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the board resolution or power of attorney is executed, with corporate seal confirmation by the foreign investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): execute before a notary; notarize the board resolution and power of attorney; obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the source state. Route B (non-Hague state): notarize and then legalize at the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the source state. Only one route may be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or equivalent constitutional document of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official registry extract, company secretary, or registered agent of the corporate UBO in the jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): certify the articles as a true copy; notarize if necessary; obtain an Apostille from the source-state competent authority. Route B (non-Hague state): notarize the certified copy; obtain consular legalization at the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the source state. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each material corporate UBO or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or corporate account-holding bank of the ultimate beneficial owner in the jurisdiction where its main bank account is maintained
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): issue the bank reference letter on bank letterhead, have the bank authorized officer signature notarized if required, then obtain an Apostille from the competent source-state authority. Route B (non-Hague state): have the bank officer's signature notarized and then obtain legalization through the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the source state. Routes must be selected exclusively and not chained.

stage_1.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening requires all UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and senior managers to be screened before formation against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UK HM Treasury consolidated list, and domestic PRC public security and PBOC sanctions/AML risk lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members, close associates, and persons identified through adverse media. Any positive hit triggers source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior AML committee escalation, and rejection unless approved by PBOC-compliant sanctions exception protocols. Daily re-screening and continuous transaction monitoring are required throughout the life of the WFOE.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration and Clearance System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), accessed through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under PRC enterprise name registration rules, a Chinese company name must contain four tiers in order: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristic, and legal form, such as administrative division plus ABC plus Cross-Border Payment Technology plus Limited Liability Company. The trade name must use standardized simplified Chinese characters; foreign corporate names may be transliterated phonetically into Pinyin or Chinese characters. The statutory Chinese name controls for all regulatory filings, while an English name may be registered as a secondary name. Transliteration must be non-misleading, free from prohibited tokens, and must not create confusion with existing registered trademarks or company names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may extend an existing name reservation online for one additional 30-day period by submitting the extension request before expiry; an expired reservation requires a fresh application. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next higher-level SAMR within 60 days of receiving the written rejection. If reconsideration upholds the rejection, the applicant may institute administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months. The applicant may also amend the rejected name and submit a new application; where rejection arises from third-party prior rights, a written consent or cancellation instrument from the earlier rights holder may cure the defect.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not acceptable for this industry. PRC company registration requires a lawful, fixed, physical registered address in China that corresponds to the actual business premises. Municipal tax authorities require an operational office with staff, books, records, and invoice equipment physically accessible during inspection. Commercial banks and SAFE/Foreign Exchange authorities reject mail-forwarding addresses for RMB and foreign-currency account opening, particularly for a licensed payment gateway WFOE with high AML risk. A shared business-center or service office may be acceptable only if it is a genuine leased office space with a real lease contract, physical occupancy, signage, and dedicated compliance personnel; a letterbox-only arrangement will be treated as non-compliant shell substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. Registered address must display a physical signboard matching the Chinese statutory company name. 2. Lease term should exceed 12 months and the premises must be zoned for commercial/IT use. 3. At least one senior compliance officer and one operations manager must be physically present during working hours. 4. The office must contain verifiable IT infrastructure, data processing or cloud-access records, payment operations documentation, and secure record storage. 5. Employee attendance, social insurance contributions, payroll, and labor contracts must match the declared headcount. Quantified risk: greater than 90% probability of unannounced on-site inspection by district-level SAMR or municipal tax authority within the first 12 months of registration due to the licensed financial/payment services classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised and adopted 29 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23 (incorporation of limited liability companies), 47 (five-year capital contribution period), 53 (board of directors), 68-69 (legal representative and executive officers), and 74 (supervisor); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC, Articles 1-31 and the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List, 2022 edition)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) acting through the local Municipal or Provincial Market Supervision Administration at the proposed WFOE registered address, and the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for the parallel Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company (Deng Ji Shen Qing Shu), together with the Foreign Investment Information Report and the Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital for general WFOE incorporation under the 2024 Company Law; shareholders specify subscribed capital in the Articles of Association and are required to pay in all subscriptions within five years from registration, unless a shorter period is required by the PBOC special payment-institution licence, which demands a paid-in registered capital of not less than RMB 100 million for nationwide online payment operations, with such capital being credited to a dedicated Chinese bank account opened after the initial company registration; no statutory blocked escrow account applies to the mere incorporation stage, but the capital cannot be withdrawn in violation of the payment-licence solvency rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, by the FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS of the Company, duly convened at the registered office on this date after the issue of the Certificate of Incorporation, as follows.
WHEREAS the shareholders have subscribed for the total registered share capital of the Company as set out in the Articles of Association, and each director has received the shareholder registry and capital schedule.
NOW BE IT RESOLVED: 1. That the incorporation and the issuance of the business licence of the Company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China are hereby ratified, and the Articles of Association, as filed with the State Administration for Market Regulation, are adopted as the supreme governance instrument of the Company. 2. That the registered share capital, consisting of fully subscribed limited liability shares, be recorded in the statutory books, and that each subscriber's obligation to contribute the agreed amount in cash or approved forms of consideration is acknowledged, with all such contributions to be made into a bank account opened in the name of the Company, and no distribution be declared before the minimum paid-in capital lawfully required by the applicable payment-institution licence and foreign exchange rules is fully satisfied. 3. That the registered office of the Company shall be the address designated in the Articles of Association and all legal notices, official correspondence and governmental writs may be served at that address and shall be effective on the date of receipt or, if refused, on the date of attempted delivery. 4. That the following officers are hereby appointed: the chairman or general manager as the statutory legal representative of the Company; one executive director; one supervisor; and, where necessary, a general manager and a finance controller, each with the authority to sign banking mandates and government filings in accordance with the operating procedures. 5. That a bank account or accounts be opened with any commercial bank duly licensed in the People's Republic of China, and that the legal representative, jointly with the finance controller and the nominated signing coordinators, be and is hereby authorized to execute all account opening forms, to give payment instructions, to sign settlement agreements, and to transact all lawful banking business relating to the Company. 6. That the Company shall thereupon obtain the Payment Business Licence from the People's Bank of China, shall submit the cross-border foreign exchange payment filing to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and shall implement all anti-money-laundering, know-your-client, transaction monitoring, card network rule compliance and risk-control procedures before processing any Visa, Mastercard or Fedwire cross-border payments. 7. That the officers and the legal representative are authorized to affix the company seal, to execute any supporting resolution, to file all statutory notices, and to engage notaries, auditors, legal counsel and consultants for completing the industrial and financial licensing matters described in the formation dossier. 8. That each director, officer and authorised signatory acts in accordance with the Articles, the governing law, the board authorisation limits and the highest standards of fiduciary duty, and that any action taken under this resolution shall be recorded in the board minutes and disclosed to the relevant regulatory authority upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Foreign Investment Negative List Clearance and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Enterprise Registration Online Portal and the concurrent MOFCOM Foreign Investment Information Report system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application, the foreign investor must verify that the proposed cross-border payment gateway scope is not on the Foreign Investment Negative List and is eligible for wholly foreign-owned status. Counsel shall then complete the online company name reservation application and select the precise business scope for online merchant acquiring, payment processing and settlement services. The beneficial ownership and identity documents of the foreign shareholder, including the certificate of incorporation, passport and director register, shall be notarized in the home jurisdiction and apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention unless otherwise exempted, and then translated into Chinese by a qualified translator. The authorised local agent or legal representative must sign the application electronically on the SAMR portal and await the pre-approval code before proceeding to submission of the formal registration dossier.
required_dossiers: SAMR company name reservation application form
Proposed Articles of Association in Chinese
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and passport copies
Notarized and apostilled identity or corporate status documents for each shareholder
Negative List compliance self-assessment with business scope explanation
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Chinese translation certificates for all non-Chinese documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected for identical or confusingly similar trade names, submit three alternative proposed names within one business day and re-file without incurring a new statutory fee. If the negative-list screening flags the business scope, amend the scope and provide a written restrictive-words compliance memo to the SAMR registration window for reconsideration before the final incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing, Articles of Association Endorsement, and Business Licence Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration under SAMR, enterprise registration hall or integrated online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation application package, including the Chinese Articles of Association, the registered-office lease agreement, the landlord's ownership title certificate, the consent of each director and supervisor, and the declaration of the legal representative, all authenticated by the foreign investor's apostilled documents. The registration window will examine the proposed registered capital, the five-year contribution schedule, the legality of the business scope, and the authority of each signatory. Upon approval, the Market Supervision Administration issues the WFOE Business Licence, which simultaneously produces the Uniform Social Credit Code. Parallel to this submission, counsel must submit the Foreign Investment Information Report to MOFCOM so that the foreign-invested enterprise status is recorded. After issuance, the company must obtain certified copies of the licence, the company seal certificate, and the preliminary articles filing record to support subsequent tax and financial licence applications.
required_dossiers: SAMR establishment registration application form signed by all shareholders
Chinese Articles of Association signed by all subscribers and endorsed by the first board
Commercial lease agreement for the registered office
Landlord ownership title deed or property right certificate
Consent and acceptance letters of directors, supervisor and legal representative
Notarized and apostilled foreign investor corporate documents and shareholder resolutions
Foreign Investment Information Report filing number and confirmation
Company seal, tax seal and financial seal card application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a deficiency correction notice, cure each listed item within ten working days by uploading amended documents or submitting notarized corrections at the service counter. If the application is suspended due to a suspected negative-list breach, provide a legal opinion of Chinese counsel confirming the permissible nature of payment gateway services and request expeditious administrative reconsideration. If the suspension continues, re-file after rectifying the business scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Statistics, Social Insurance, Bank Account and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (SAT) local tax bureau, National Bureau of Statistics, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, People's Bank of China designated clearing registering bank, and SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days of obtaining the Business Licence, the legal representative must complete the taxpayer registration through the electronic tax service, register the corporate accounting system, and obtain the taxpayer identification status for VAT, enterprise income tax, stamp duty and withholding obligations. The company must simultaneously register its payroll under the national social insurance portal and open a RMB basic deposit account in its registered name. After the basic bank account is activated, the company must complete the SAFE foreign investor registration for outward remittances and inward capital settlement, and any foreign currency operational account for Visa, Mastercard and Fedwire settlement. The paid-in capital must be verified by a Chinese certified public accountant if required by the PBOC payment licence application, and the capital contribution records must be filed at the same registration window.
required_dossiers: WFOE Business Licence (original and certified copy)
Uniform Social Credit Code certificate
Tax registration declaration form and enterprise information form
Registered office lease and business licence address consistency proof
Legal representative ID card or passport copy and company seal sample
Bank basic account certificate and SAFE foreign exchange registration application
Articles of Association and board resolution on capital contribution
Payroll roster, social insurance registration form and employment consent forms
Capital verification or audit report prepared by a PRC certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a late-filing penalty, submit a written explanation and a waiver request supported by evidence of force majeure or governmental portal downtime. If SAFE returns the foreign exchange registration as incomplete, correct the capital contribution and shareholding schedule and resubmit through the designated bank. If social insurance registration is queried, provide the employment contracts and proof of benefit enrolment within one week; failure to remedy may trigger automatic administrative penalty, so a cure plan should be filed immediately upon receipt of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment Business Licence Application under PBOC and Cross-Border Payment Registration with SAFE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) Payment Services and Licensing Department, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Cross-Border Payment Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After all post-incorporation filings are complete, counsel must prepare a comprehensive payment-institution application dossier demonstrating legal management, shareholder solvency, a detailed anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing programme, information security architecture, transaction monitoring, settlement risk controls, business continuity planning, irregularity reporting and customer protection processes. The application must include the paid-in capital verification report, internal audit conclusions, technical infrastructure description and the proposed cross-border settlement flow through Visa and Mastercard and Fedwire correspondents. The company must also formally file the cross-border foreign exchange payment institution information report with SAFE and obtain the card network association or sponsorship approval required for direct acquiring. Once the PBOC licence is granted, the company must interconnect the transaction monitoring system with the PBOC payment information supervision platform and obtain a production go-live permission before processing live payments.
required_dossiers: PBOC Non-bank Payment Institution Licensing application form
Business Licence, Articles of Association and minutes of all shareholder resolutions
Audited financial statements and paid-in capital verification report
Anti-money-laundering compliance programme and officer appointment notice
Information security policy, penetration testing report and business continuity plan
Cross-border payment flow, settlement account and custody arrangement description
SAFE cross-border foreign exchange payment institution filing form
Card network agreements or sponsor bank letter confirming Visa/Mastercard clearing access
RISK assessment and internal control certification by a PRC qualified auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the PBOC issues a refusal or supplementary inquiry, correct all stated deficiencies and resubmit an amended dossier within six months without payment of a new licensing fee. If SAFE suspends cross-border payment filing, revise the payment flow to comply with the settlement and repatriation rules, present a corrective remediation plan, and seek administrative review of any adverse PBOC decision before the PBOC administrative reconsideration committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) Payment Licensing Division, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Cross-Border Payment Supervision Department; no municipal industrial licensing board applies because ISIC 6619 is a purely digital payment-related financial service, not a manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Payment Business Licence for Non-bank Payment Institutions issued under the PBOC Administrative Measures for Payment Services and the Cross-Border Foreign Exchange Payment Institution Approval of SAFE, together with Visa and Mastercard acquiring programme registration and Fedwire settlement gateway approval.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable. The target business is pure digital payment and consulting financial processing under ISIC 6619 with no physical manufacturing, chemical production, assembly line, industrial plant or warehouse and therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration dossier is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The activity generates no wastewater, no volatile organic compound emissions, no hazardous waste, no air emissions and no contaminated stormwater streams; only general municipal office refuse from a leased office space may arise and that is handled by the building's licensed commercial waste contractor.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A Fire Safety Certificate under the PRC Fire Protection Law is required for the leased office as a place of work, and the local Emergency Management Bureau will verify basic fire-door, emergency-exit, extinguisher and detector compliance; structural load inspection is not applicable because the facility is a non-industrial office; workplace safety registration and mandatory occupational health filings must nevertheless be completed for all employees in accordance with the national Work Safety Law, including the appointment of a safety officer and a written emergency evacuation plan, before the PBOC payment licence can allow physical or systems operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic portal: National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) accessible at etax.chinatax.gov.cn and through provincial-level electronic tax bureaus; local competent tax authority is the district/county STA office for the WFOE's registered address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign shareholders incorporate the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Business License and Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the national legal entity identifier. Step 2: Within 30 days of business license issuance, complete tax identification registration by using the USCC and legal representative credentials on the provincial e-Tax portal or at the competent STA office; this registration creates the taxpayer profile and binds the USCC as the TIN for all STA filings. Step 3: Complete VAT taxpayer registration, selecting status under the VAT regime (initially small-scale or general VAT taxpayer), electronic invoice quota, and invoice issuance method. Step 4: Register for payroll/social insurance withholding, corporate income tax, withholding income tax on non-resident shareholders, stamp duty, and any service-related taxes. Step 5: Report bank account details to the STA within 15 days after account opening. Step 6: If cross-border exporting or zero-rated or exempt supplies are claimed, complete customs export enterprise registration and cross-border service filing through the integrated electronic customs and tax systems, and link export tax refund qualification with the export collection records of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). The WFOE itself is a Chinese resident enterprise; no non-resident TIN is needed for the entity. Foreign shareholders require Chinese TINs or withholding-identity registration only when filing withholding taxes and treaty relief claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, taxed on worldwide net income at a 25% statutory CIT rate; there is no pass-through treatment; dividends distributed to offshore shareholders are separately subject to Chinese withholding at 10%, subject to applicable double tax treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. China has no elective pass-through regime for a limited liability company; a WFOE is mandatorily classified as a Chinese resident entity-level taxpayer. Under tax treaties, the WFOE may apply for treaty benefits as a PRC resident and beneficial owner with respect to its foreign parent, but this is a treaty eligibility determination, not a domestic entity-classification election. No consolidated or fiscal unity election is available for related limited liability companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Provisional Regulations on VAT, administered nationally by the STA and Ministry of Finance; China's general headline goods rate is 13%, construction and transport-related services are 9%, and payment, clearing and financial/modern services supplied domestically by a payment gateway are 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration threshold; however, any Chinese entity carrying on taxable activities is required to complete VAT basic registration from commencement of business regardless of turnover. Small-scale taxpayers with current monthly sales up to RMB 100,000 or quarterly sales up to RMB 300,000 may qualify for a VAT exemption, but that temporary exemption does not displace the registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under Golden Tax Phase IV (Jin Shui IV) and the national e-Invoice Service Platform, all VAT invoices, including fully digital electronic invoices, must be issued in real time through the STA-controlled e-invoice system using API or web-based issuance; invoices carry a unique 20-digit invoice code, a dynamic QR code, and an encrypted digital signature. VAT special invoices are subject to quota and must be matched and reconciled through the STA VAT Invoice Management System before the buyer can claim input VAT credit. The system performs real-time invoice data upload, fiscal clearance, purchase and sale anomaly scanning, and anti-fraud controls on high-risk taxpayers; pre-printed paper blank invoices are no longer permissible for fully digitalized taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For cross-border services, including payment gateway and merchant acquiring services, zero-rating meaning a 0% VAT rate with input VAT credit or refund is available only where the service falls within the STA cross-border zero-rate catalogue, including certain international transportation, research and development, technology, software, and information services, and all statutory conditions are satisfied. For payment and clearing services supplied to an overseas bank, acquirer, payment network, or foreign financial institution and wholly consumed outside mainland China, the usual treatment is cross-border VAT exemption without input-VAT refund, rather than zero-rating, unless the WFOE can establish that the service qualifies under the zero-rated catalogue provision for its specific service code. To claim zero-rating or cross-border exemption, the WFOE must demonstrate that: (a) the service recipient is a non-resident enterprise or individual located outside China; (b) the service is not used for domestic onshore settlement, domestic payment acceptance, or domestic trade facilitation; (c) the cross-border service agreement, transaction logs, payment gateway fee statements, and invoices clearly identify the offshore principal and the foreign-currency consideration; (d) the revenue is booked as cross-border service export revenue and included in SAFE trade-in-services monitoring; and (e) the digital e-invoice is issued with the correct cross-border zero-rate or exemption label and the relevant statutory contract number where required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration is not applicable to cross-border payment gateway services; no physical goods Bill of Entry or Bill of Lading is required for service exports.

Signed cross-border payment gateway service agreement between the WFOE and the overseas bank, acquirer, payment network, or foreign financial institution, clearly defining service scope, fees, and destination of service consumption.

Foreign exchange collection voucher from a Chinese bank, equivalent to an inward remittance certificate, or the SAFE trade-in-services export collection record evidencing the actual receipt of offshore fees from the foreign counterparty.

Commercial invoice or full digital electronic invoice carrying the cross-border zero-rate or exemption status label and the relevant cross-border service code, where exemption or zero-rating is claimed.

Payment transaction logs and monthly merchant settlement reports showing that the gateway services are provided to foreign financial institutions for offshore transactions and are not facilitating domestic Chinese payment acceptance.

Certificate of foreign residence or identity of the non-resident service recipient, and, if treaty benefits are claimed, a beneficial ownership declaration or tax-residence certificate of the foreign party.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA will scrutinize zero-rating and cross-border exemption claims through Golden Tax Phase IV data analytics, matching the cross-border service contract, digital e-invoice labels, SAFE foreign exchange receipts, bank settlement records, and the non-resident status of the overseas beneficiary. Failure to substantiate the export nature of the service or any material misrepresentation triggers: (i) immediate removal of the zero-rate or exemption treatment and reclassification as a domestic taxable payment service at 6% VAT; (ii) mandatory repayment of all VAT input credits claimed or refunded, plus late-payment interest from the original filing date; (iii) a civil penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law; (iv) criminal exposure for fraudulent export tax refunds under Article 204 of the Criminal Law where wilful deception or fictitious cross-border contracts are established; and (v) SAFE monetary penalties and potential revocation of cross-border payment or foreign-exchange qualification. The statutory clawback period may extend to 10 years for fraudulent and false export-refund and zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with a dual-track currency control framework. Renminbi is unconditionally convertible on current account items such as trade in goods and services, dividends, and interest, provided the underlying transaction is commercial and backed by valid documentation. Capital account items, including foreign direct investment (FDI), intercompany loans, equity transfers, and outward remittances for acquisitions, are subject to filing, registration, or approval with SAFE. A foreign-owned payment gateway entity will experience friction when moving large inbound equity injections and outbound service fee settlements: every remittance must be matched to a registered contract, invoice, and tax clearance certificate. Surrender or repatriation of export proceeds is no longer mandatory; however, all foreign currency receipts must be lodged with a designated domestic bank in the foreign exchange account regime and can be retained, converted to RMB on demand, or used to pay imported inputs within the verified scope of the trade credit system. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders requires a prior year audited financial statement, corporate income tax settlement certificate, and board resolution declaring dividends, and the entire process is subject to anti-money laundering and sanctions screening by the settlement bank. The SAFE system also applies periodic dynamic verification of business registers, and any deviation from the filed business scope will block funds flows. For a high-risk ISIC 6619 payment company, the bank will review the legal basis of each capital movement under the Payment Services Measures and the Cross-Border Payment Business guidelines, creating stringent know-your-transaction gateways before any conversion or disbursement is executed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to China within 90 days of the stated shipment date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the statutory surrender requirement was abolished in 2007. However, all foreign exchange receipts must be reported and deposited into the exporter's designated foreign exchange settlement account, and any conversion into Renminbi must follow SAFE's real-transaction-background rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Airwallex, or Currencycloud) are legally barred from directly onboarding a Chinese Mainland corporate entity, as non-bank payment service providers must hold a Payment Business Administrative License issued by the PBOC and join the NetsUnion or UnionPay clearing network. Any cross-border service must be delivered through a licensed Chinese bank or a licensed third-party payment institution (e.g., Alibaba's Alipay or Tencent's Tenpay) acting as a gateway. An offshore EMI may only provide ancillary technology or reporting solutions, never hold segregated client funds inside China. Feasibility rating: Low for direct vaulting and settlement; Medium for indirect API integration into a Chinese bank's foreign exchange and clearing infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly established WFOE, the statutory legal representative (or a duly appointed local director) must appear physically before the bank's corporate account opening committee, together with the company seal and the complete corporate kit. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for high-risk payment entities; however, a local manager with a notarized power of attorney from the overseas board can substitute for the statutory representative if the power of attorney is apostilled or consular legalized and the support staff undergo an in-person identification and anti-money laundering interview at the branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) obscurity in a multi-layer offshore holding chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain charts showing all intermediate shell and holding companies, certified copies of registration certificates, board resolutions, UBO declaration forms signed by each shareholder, and a deposition of origin of wealth supported by audited financial statements for the prior 3 years. For any nominee shareholder, provide a formal nominee disclosure and a no-beneficial-interest statutory declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment gateway business scope ambiguity under ISIC 6619, presenting P2P money-transfer risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 27001 certification and a copy of the PBOC payment business license (where required), a transaction monitoring policy document that includes real-time screening against UN sanctions and PEP lists, a corporate risk appetite statement, and a third-party audit report confirming that all merchant classification codes match the actual merchant business line and that no crypto-to-fiat conversion is executed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High frequency of cross-border transactions to high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., tax havens or sanctioned neighbors) without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A marketable commercial contract and invoice file for each corridor, including Incoterms, shipping or service delivery evidence, logistics bills of lading or system usage logs, as well as the counterparty's KYC pack and a description of the routing logic used to select the receiving bank. Provide a geographic heat-map of expected payment flows and a modeled sanctions false-positive resolution procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient proof of inward capital injection and dividend repatriation capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate, capital verification report issued by a licensed Chinese CPA, original Foreign Currency Capital Account opening notice, the actual-to-target capital contribution schedule, and for dividends: goodwill tax settlement certificate, independent audit report, tax clearance letter, and a board resolution declaring the distribution. Also include a reconciliation of the injected capital to the paid-in capital ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injection from the overseas parent, the WFOE must open a foreign currency capital account with a SAFE-designated bank, file the FDI information with the bank portal, and receive funds via SWIFT with purpose code 'FDI Capital Injection (FDI/DEBIT)' (or chase code 1100 as per the General Data Format of Cross-border Trade). After funds arrival, a CPA must issue a capital verification report and the sum is then converted to RMB with a bank duty of matching the exchange rate against the central parity. All remittance messages must include the entity's unified social credit code and the contract / registration reference number, otherwise the bank will quarantine the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement outflows are executed primarily through (a) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for service fees and technology licensing payments, (b) irrevocable commercial letters of credit (L/C at sight or usance) for merchandise imports, and (c) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for lower-value open-account purchase orders. For payments to overseas merchants in the PSP business, the company will aggregate the settlement into daily RMB clearance and then convert to USD/GBP via the designated bank's FX desk, subject to SAFE's cross-border commercial invoice matching and annual quota supervision. Each payment requires a valid commercial contract, invoice, and customs or logistics evidence for goods, or a service provision log and beneficial tax declaration for services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore licensing: CNY/USD plain-vanilla forwards, plain-vanilla FX swaps and cross-currency swaps are permitted for genuine commercial hedging, with a maximum tenor of 12 months renewable.

NDF windows: Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDF) may only be executed through offshore subsidiaries or via a specially approved location-based bank window for hedging the CNY exposure of cross-border trade, but an onshore WFOE cannot directly enter NDF contracts with unlicensed providers.
Options: Limited FX covered calls and puts with premium borne against invoice values are permissible, but naked speculative positions are strictly prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Report (Annual Return) and Publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing by June 30: automatic inclusion in SAMR List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations from July 1; failure to rectify within 3 years leads to classification as a Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise and may trigger administrative cancellation/revocation of registration. False or misleading disclosures expose the company to administrative fines and credit punishment under the Enterprise Information Disclosure Regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Reconciliation Return and Settlement Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the local tax bureau in the WFOE registration jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the following tax year (fiscal year ends December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the CIT return: administrative fine up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 10,000 in serious cases, under the Tax Administration and Levy Collection Law. Underpayment from June 1 accrues daily late-payment interest/surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Evasion or fraudulent supporting books may result in penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, asset preservation, tax registration deactivation, public credit downgrade and potential transfer to criminal authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the SAMR enterprise information system for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false reporting: MOFCOM/SAMR issues a correction order requiring remediation within a fixed period; refusal to correct allows an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 under the Foreign Investment Law and supporting implementing regulations. The violation is also recorded in the enterprise credit record and may impair foreign-exchange and banking renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Information Confirmation in SAMR Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the Market Entity Beneficial Owner Information Registration framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must accompany the SAMR annual report filed between January 1 and June 30; any change in UBO, shareholding, control or voting rights must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false UBO confirmation: SAMR orders correction; continued non-compliance may result in administrative penalties, inclusion in abnormal operation list, credit blacklisting, and restrictions on equity change registration. For licensed cross-border payment entities, PBOC AML inspections may additionally revoke senior manager fit-and-proper approvals or freeze license renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Certified CPA Audit Report of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR (submitted as a supporting file with the annual report) and State Taxation Administration (retained with tax records); PBOC receives the audited financial statements for payment-license supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed no later than June 30 to accompany the annual report; PBOC payment institution audited financial statements due within 4 months after fiscal year end (April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have annual financial statements audited violates PRC Company Law; SAMR will treat the annual report as non-compliant, exposing the WFOE to abnormal-operation listing and credit punishment. A qualified, adverse, or disclaimer audit opinion gives PBOC/SAFE cause to review the payment license, require corrective action, or suspend cross-border settlement permissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PBOC Payment Institution Annual Report and AML/CFT Compliance Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) Payment Services Supervision Division and local PBOC branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year (April 30); AML institutional reports due according to PBOC filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance can trigger PBOC corrective orders, monetary penalties under the Measures for the Administration of Payment Services, suspension of payment business lines, restrictions on cross-border settlement, and revocation of the Payment Service License in severe cases. AML/CFT deficiencies also create concurrent SAFE enforcement exposure for the cross-border payment gateway.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold exempts a PRC limited liability company from independent audit. Under the PRC Company Law, every company must prepare annual financial reports and engage licensed CPAs to audit them; accordingly, this WFOE is mandated to carry out an annual audit regardless of whether total assets, annual revenue, or employee count falls below any arbitrary level. Additionally, PBOC-licensed payment institutions are subject to mandatory annual audit and special AML/financial statement review irrespective of scale or transactional volume.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE) issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially converged with IFRS; small and micro enterprises may apply the Standard for Small Business Enterprises; the WFOE cross-border payment scope will generally require full CAS, with consolidated/regulatory reporting reconciled to IFRS or US GAAP if the overseas parent group requires it. CIT returns must reconcile accounting profit to taxable income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must register its ultimate beneficial owner(s) with SAMR using the 25% equity/voting threshold or actual-control standard, confirm UBO data in every SAMR annual report, and file any change in shareholding, directorship, control, or beneficial ownership within 30 days of the transaction or event. Cross-border payment gateways must also maintain enhanced customer-and-counterparty UBO information for PBOC AML and SAFE cross-border inspections. Failure to comply with SAMR UBO confirmation or the 30-day change-reporting window is ground for correction orders, fines, credit blacklisting, and suspension of the payment-service license.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Statutory Minute Book (Shareholders, Board, and Senior Management Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 10,000 per year for a WFOE with cross-border payment activities and consolidated-group audit requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% EIT rate for qualified High/New Technology Enterprises; additional 100% super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure; 10% preferential rate for qualifying advanced integrated circuit enterprises and certain software enterprises; 15% encouraged-industry rate in Hainan Free Trade Port; small-and-low-profit enterprise progressive rate reductions as applicable to eligible WFOE operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) together with Form A105000 (Related Party Transactions Report) and supporting schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic filing portal using the enterprise digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filing plus annual reconciliation
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns must be filed within 15 days after each quarter-end; the annual corporate income tax return and related-party transaction schedules must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, normally 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business revenue from the cross-border payment gateway operation, including merchant acquiring commissions, card scheme fees billed to merchants, settlement processing charges, currency conversion margins, and any float interest retained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross turnover attributable to the Chinese WFOE only; do not include customer/merchant settlement funds held in pass-through accounts as revenue. The WFOE must distinguish commission fees from fiduciary settlement balances and support revenue with issued VAT invoices and merchant statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs directly attributable to revenue generation, such as acquiring bank fees, Visa/Mastercard scheme fees, gateway infrastructure hosting, software licences, telecommunication costs, staff payroll and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border intercompany costs must be supported by contracts, actual services, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; rice-invoice-only arrangements will be disregarded. Cost allocation from the foreign parent to the Chinese WFOE must reflect arm's length benefit received by the Chinese taxable entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges excluding corporate income tax, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp tax, and other deductible turnover-based taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT collected on cross-border payment services is not an income tax deductible item in this box except as included in business costs; the WFOE should separately file VAT through the e-Tax system. Stamp tax on cross-border contracts may be deductible if properly assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses, including salaries, rent, professional fees, marketing, IT security, KYC and AML compliance expenses, and intercompany management/service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany fees paid to non-resident shareholders are deductible only to the extent the services were actually rendered, the WFOE obtained an economic or commercial benefit, and a Chinese TP policy and service agreement exist. Related-party interest deductions are capped under thin capitalization rules (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for financial enterprises or 1:1 otherwise).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit or loss computed as Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3 minus Box 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is the starting point for Chinese corporate income tax on domestic and worldwide income. The WFOE as a resident enterprise is taxed on worldwide income, but must ensure no non-resident shareholder's income is mistakenly included as the WFOE's taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of non-deductible expenses, excess related-party interest, entertainment expenses over statutory limits, penalties and fines; deduction of tax holidays, R&D super-deduction, carried-forward losses and treaty-consistent adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule A105000 for all related-party transactions with non-resident parties, including service fees, royalties and interest. Non-deductible penalties and bribery-related payments must be added back. Loss carryforward is limited to 5 taxable years for ordinary operating losses, with strict continuity-of-business substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and final income tax payable after applying the 25% headline rate, offsetting quarterly prepayments, and computing balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any dividend distribution declared out of after-tax profits to a non-resident parent is not deductible against EIT liability and triggers a separate 10% profit repatriation withholding tax, subject to treaty relief. The WFOE must not use the Box 7 net tax payable as a substitute for dividend withholding tax reporting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of quarterly or annual EIT returns triggers a fine of up to CNY 2,000, or CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 for serious cases, under Article 62 of the Tax Collection Administration Law. Late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the outstanding tax. False declarations, underreporting of revenue, fabricating related-party transactions, or fraudulent use of treaty benefits constitute tax evasion under Article 63, exposing the taxpayer to a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and, when criminal thresholds are met, criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to 7 years for deliberate non-payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on outbound dividends paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise beneficiary; treaty-reduced rates may apply, commonly 5% where the beneficial owner holds directly and continuously at least 25% of the capital of the paying enterprise and meets the anti-abuse tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction for the relevant year, execute a declaration of beneficial ownership, and submit the TRC plus supporting substance documentation to the Chinese withholding agent before remittance. The withholding agent or non-resident may apply to the Chinese tax authority for reduced treaty withholding; where tax has already been withheld at 10%, the non-resident may claim a refund within three years from the original assessment date. Beneficial ownership is tested under SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9, requiring business substance, genuine decision-making, risk absorption, and absence of conduit arrangements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 10% on outbound royalties and 10% on outbound interest paid to non-residents, plus VAT at 6% on taxable royalty and technical-service imports unless an exemption applies. Under applicable bilateral tax treaties, royalty rates are typically reduced to 5% or 10%, and interest rates to 7% or 10%, depending on the treaty partner and the nature of the IP; China-Hong Kong and China-Singapore DTAs commonly allow 5% on qualified royalties and 7% on qualified interest where beneficial ownership is proved.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File contemporaneous documentation must be prepared when annual related-party tangible property transfers exceed CNY 200 million, intangible property or financial asset transfers exceed CNY 100 million, or other related-party transactions (service fees, royalties, interest) exceed CNY 40 million; Master File documentation is required where the MNE group's prior-year consolidated revenue exceeds CNY 2 billion and the Chinese entity has related-party transactions, or where annual related-party transactions reported by the Chinese entity exceed CNY 1 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the State Taxation Administration applies economic substance doctrine through the beneficial ownership test, substance-over-form principles, and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in EIT Law Article 47. For a cross-border payment gateway WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities must be performed in China, including merchant underwriting, KYC/AML controls, transaction monitoring, currency conversion decisions, settlement instructions, system risk management, and board-level decision-making; the entity must maintain local employees, office premises, business licences, bank settlement accounts, and payment scheme approvals sufficient to demonstrate that profits are economically connected to local activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is established as a thin-capitalised shell with no office, no staff, and no local decision-making, yet it holds the payment gateway licence and collects billions of RMB of merchant settlement funds; all profit is stripped out annually as inflated service fees, management fees, or intra-group charges to a foreign parent, leaving zero taxable profit in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 6, 41 and 47 permit the tax authority to recharacterise the arrangement under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, adjust taxable income on an arm's length basis, impose a 10% deemed dividend WHT, and apply late-payment interest. Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 imposes an additional penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, and 0.05% daily late payment surcharges accrue on any adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Chinese courts may pierce the corporate veil where directors deliberately operated the WFOE as a mere instrumentality and stripped assets; directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and creditor losses, subjected to asset seizure and travel restriction/blacklisting orders, and criminally indicted for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, carrying up to 7 years' imprisonment in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE reports artificially low margins by allocating excessive costs to related-party merchants acquiring services, using an unsubstantiated TNMM with a loss-making tested party, failing to prepare the required Local File/Master File, and refusing to disclose cross-border payment service contracts and settlement routing data to the SAT during audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 41 empowers the tax authority to make a transfer pricing adjustment based on the best available data and to add interest; SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42 requires contemporaneous documentation at the statutory thresholds. Under Tax Collection Administration Law Articles 62 and 63, failure to provide required related-party documentation carries administrative fines of CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000, while deliberate concealment of related-party transactions can be treated as tax evasion with penalties of 50% to 500% of the understated tax and criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false related-party declaration filings may be personally investigated for aiding tax evasion, face civil restitution to the WFOE and minority shareholders, have their personal bank accounts frozen and exit visas blocked through the tax credit blacklisting system, and be imprisoned for up to 7 years if the scheme was used to deliberately defraud the state of material tax amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial Ownership Misrepresentation and Abusive Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Outbound dividends, interest, or royalties are routed through a Hong Kong, Singapore, or other low-tax conduit company that lacks real staff, premises, and decision-making power, solely to claim a reduced 5% DTA WHT rate on profit generated by the Chinese payment gateway and evade the statutory 10% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SAT will deny treaty benefits under the beneficial ownership rules in SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 and under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in EIT Law Article 47; the under-withheld difference is collected as a 10% WHT deficiency plus daily interest. Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 permits assessment of a 50% to 500% penalty on the tax evaded, and Article 201 of the Criminal Law applies where intentional non-withholding and false beneficial ownership certifications are used as a revenue fraud scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE and the conduit entity may be jointly liable for the uncollected WHT, ordered to restore distributed assets, subjected to personal travel bans and blacklisting in China's tax credit system, and criminally prosecuted for fraudulent tax filings and false treaty claims; conviction can lead to serious criminal sanctions including imprisonment for tax evasion offenses, plus civil damages to the Chinese revenue authority and ultimate shareholders who suffered exposure from the abusive structure.
